title: Lesson 37: Asynchronous Apex: Batch, Queueable, Scheduled, and Future, and How to Choose
description: How to choose between future methods, queueable Apex, batch Apex, and scheduled Apex on evidence rather than habit, and why all four draw from one shared asynchronous budget.

questions.question: A nightly job must process tens of thousands of records in chunks, keep a running total, and pick up failures on the next run. Which primitive and pattern fit?
options: A single future method that iterates every record, since it gets its own transaction.
One queueable job per record, so each record's retry is isolated on its own.
A scheduled class that performs the work directly, since scheduled code is async.
Batch Apex with a stateful counter, started by a schedulable, plus a retry flag.
questions.explanation: Batch Apex handles volume with chunk-level fault isolation, a stateful counter carries the total across chunks, and a flag on each record lets the next run pick up failures; the scheduler only starts it.

questions.question: A design enqueues one asynchronous job per record while iterating a large query. Why is this a problem?
options: Async capacity is a shared org-level budget, so cost scales with record count.
Each job runs in its own transaction, which is the safest option for isolation.
Async limits are allocated per feature, so one job per record cannot affect others.
Queueable jobs cannot accept sObjects, so the design will not compile at all.
questions.explanation: Asynchronous capacity is an org-level budget shared with every other feature, so a job per record multiplies the shared cost by the record count and hits the per-transaction enqueue cap.

questions.question: What is the correct job of a scheduled class?
options: Running heavy queries and callouts itself, since it runs asynchronously.
Holding the trigger time and handing off to a batch job or a queueable.
Carrying large record collections between runs using persisted instance state.
Replacing batch Apex entirely for any large-volume processing need.
questions.explanation: The scheduler answers when, not how: it runs under tight synchronous-style limits, so its body should hand off to a batch job or a queueable where the real work and higher budget live.
